knowledge_gaps: The residual lies in [-0.1, 0.1], so its direct effect on a pairwise score difference is at most 0.2. Its scale relative to baseline candidate-score gaps is unmeasured; training margins against individual negatives cannot establish whether it can change top-10 rankings.

Registering an unused attention table in the pooling control matches stored parameters, not effective capacity or computation. Tying candidate queries and history keys also imposes symmetric attention similarity, although the value/target transition score remains asymmetric.

Reproduction requires explicit initialization, normalization epsilon, branch regularization, optimizer groups, all-padding softmax behavior, and scoring dispatch. Tensor shapes alone cannot distinguish aligned B×L targets from B×C candidates when C=L.

Baseline timing does not establish the candidate-attention configuration's feasible epoch cap. Candidate-dependent training costs, checkpoint retention, and a deterministic fallback for budget exhaustion need specification.

The report omits paired validation uncertainty and selection optimism. Sparse independent embedding tables may overfit frequent transitions, and ID-only attention cannot establish semantic specificity. The proposed ratings remain subjective; implementation difficulty may be understated.
